conclusions.claim: All nine utilities resolve helper location from their own __file__ under Python -I in an unrelated cwd without adding import paths.
conclusions.evidence: Actual bounded module initialization passed with PATH Git and an explicit path containing spaces and shell metacharacters; cwd stdlib/helper trap files were not imported.

conclusions.claim: Invalid overrides do not fall back, and missing PATH does not implicitly use defaults.
conclusions.evidence: Missing/broken explicit targets and bare-name overrides with absent PATH failed before post-bootstrap work.

conclusions.claim: Only Git bootstrap wiring changed the nine utilities executable logic.
conclusions.evidence: AST comparison against pre-fix commit 64515dc5f0cb707552bfd0e9ed89a97f61fc6fca equals original after removing the new runpy import and restoring original GIT assignment.

conclusions.claim: All historical verification main functions now pass against current project state.
conclusions.evidence: Main functions deliberately not executed; expected historical revisions/inputs remain as previously authored.

scope: Independent scratch executables, isolated real-script bootstrap only, read-only Git and AST comparison. No main function, document builder, deliverable or scientific analysis executed.
limits: Bootstrap probes deliberately stop every utility immediately after Git initialization.
Historical main functions retain their original expected revisions and inputs.
A successful version prefix is a suitability check, not cryptographic executable authentication; later executable replacement is outside scope.
This review confirms Git discovery/bootstrap and preserved executable AST; it does not rerun scientific pipelines, Lean proofs, archived verification bodies or document generation.
